name: Linear Diophantine equations and the Frobenius number
formula: ax + by = c \text{ has integer solutions} \iff \gcd(a, b) \mid c; \qquad a, b > 0,\ \gcd(a, b) = 1 \implies \text{largest } N \ne ax + by\ (x, y \ge 0) \text{ is } ab - a - b
whenToUse: Coins or packages of two sizes, integer solutions of a linear equation, or the largest total that cannot be made from two amounts.
example: $6x + 15y = 40$ has no integer solutions, since $3 \nmid 40$. With stamps worth $5$ and $8$, the largest total that cannot be made is $40 - 5 - 8 = 27$, and $\frac{(5-1)(8-1)}{2} = 14$ totals cannot be made at all.
pitfall: The Frobenius formula needs nonnegative amounts and coprime sizes. Once one solution $(x, y)$ is found, the others are $\left(x + \frac{b}{g}t,\ y - \frac{a}{g}t\right)$ with $g = \gcd(a, b)$.
